items.title: Senate Panel Holds Fauci in Contempt of Congress
items.author: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
items.content: <article>Dr. Anthony Fauci had refused to answer questions at a hearing last week, invoking the Fifth Amendment. Republicans argued that he wasn’t entitled to that protection because he had a presidential pardon.</article>

items.title: Senate Panel Votes to Hold Fauci in Contempt
items.author: Jan Hoffman
items.content: <article>The case is unique, legal scholars say, because of the tension between the Fifth Amendment and the reach of a presidential pardon. The potential consequences could be grave.</article>

items.title: El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate Primary Win Sets Up the Left’s Biggest Test of the Fall
items.author: Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate candidacy poses a critical challenge for Democrats’ ascendant progressive wing: Can an insurgent candidate, with unabashedly liberal positions, win a general election in a moderate state?</article>

items.title: Tennessee’s Andy Ogles Faces Well-Funded Opposition in House Primary Thursday
items.author: Patricia Mazzei, Tim Balk and Emily Cochrane
items.content: <article>Representative Andy Ogles received President Trump’s endorsement, but his challenger, Charlie Hatcher, a former state agriculture commissioner, has the backing of Gov. Bill Lee.</article>

items.title: F.D.A. Approves Moderna’s mRNA Flu Vaccine
items.author: Christina Jewett
items.content: <article>The agency had initially refused to even review the application but reversed course after a public outcry.</article>

items.title: C.I.A. Sets Up Secret Cuba Task Force as Trump Pressures Havana
items.author: Adam Entous
items.content: <article>The task force will allow the spy agency to quickly direct more financial, human and technical resources at the island, with the goal of creating fissures among the Cuban political elite.</article>

items.title: After Michigan Loss, AIPAC Weighs a Second Effort to Defeat El-Sayed
items.author: Jennifer Medina and Theodore Schleifer
items.content: <article>The pro-Israel organization spent $32 million in an unsuccessful effort to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary. It might try again in the general election.</article>

items.title: Federal Judge Weakens The National Firearms Act
items.author: Chris Cameron
items.content: <article>The National Firearms Act mandated a permitting process for short-barreled rifles and shotguns, as well as suppressors. A judge ruled that the provision was unconstitutional.</article>

items.title: Mayor Says El-Sayed’s Win Shows He Is More Than a ‘Mini-Mamdani’
items.author: Jeffery C. Mays
items.content: <article>Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York said that Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s close victory in the Michigan Senate primary put “working-class Americans back at the heart of our politics.”</article>

items.title: Trump-Backed Michigan Candidate Loses Primary to Rival Who Suspended His Campaign
items.author: Bayliss Wagner
items.content: <article>Without running a single ad or filing a campaign finance report, Tom Smith, who had suspended his bid, soundly defeated Amir Hassan, a Navy veteran backed by President Trump.</article>

items.title: Bunny Dolls and Disturbing Allegations: Max Miller’s Strange CNN Interview
items.author: Michael M. Grynbaum
items.content: <article>In a 23-minute appearance with the anchor Jake Tapper, the Ohio Republican made an unusual effort to rebut a multitude of allegations that have threatened his re-election bid.</article>

items.title: Scandal Leaves North Carolina G.O.P. With No Candidate and Little Time
items.author: Eduardo Medina
items.content: <article>Representative Chuck Edwards’s decision to drop his re-election bid amid sexual harassment charges came as a Democratic farmer, Jamie Ager, was already making inroads.</article>

items.title: Senate Confirms Dr. Erica Schwartz as C.D.C. Director
items.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
items.content: <article>Dr. Schwartz, a deputy surgeon general in the first Trump administration, has publicly supported childhood vaccines.</article>

items.title: Why Polling Overestimated Abdul El-Sayed’s Advantage in Michigan
items.author: Ruth Igielnik
items.content: <article>Surveys greatly overestimated how Dr. Abdul El-Sayed would fare in the state’s Democratic Senate primary, revealing some typical polling challenges.</article>

items.title: U.S. Cuts Ties With Organ Donor Group After Reports of Abuses
items.author: Brian M. Rosenthal
items.content: <article>The federal government is ending its contract with a Kentucky nonprofit that it says pressured medical workers to remove organs from patients who were getting better.</article>

items.title: Francesca Hong Said Thanksgiving Should Be Canceled. Can Wisconsin Voters Forgive Her?
items.author: Julie Bosman
items.content: <article>“Cancel Thanksgiving,” she wrote. “VDay” brings out “the worst of humanity,” she mused. Francesca Hong’s old social media posts get a fresh look ahead of Wisconsin’s Democratic primary for governor.</article>

items.title: El-Sayed Got a Big Win for the Left. Can It Win Like This Nationally?
items.author: Nate Cohn
items.content: <article>The new activist left is built on a coalition that may be too narrow to thrive in Democratic primaries in other areas, particularly the South.</article>

items.title: Cost of Trump’s Namesake Warships Likely to Rise by 50 Percent or More
items.author: John Ismay
items.content: <article>President Trump’s goal of building a “golden fleet” of 15 battleships could cost $275 billion, according to a government estimate.</article>

items.title: Where El-Sayed Showed Strengths, and Weaknesses, in the Michigan Primary
items.author: Katie Glueck, Caroline Soler and Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>Dr. Abdul El-Sayed had a strong showing in college towns, while Representative Haley Stevens did well in Black urban centers.</article>

items.title: Abdul El-Sayed’s Winning New Political Uniform
items.author: Vanessa Friedman
items.content: <article>Could the black T-shirt and jeans be the next big thing in Washington?</article>

items.title: Why Congress Wants a Closer U.S.-Israel Defense Partnership
items.author: Robert Jimison
items.content: <article>A proposal making its way through Congress would integrate the U.S. and Israeli defense and intelligence apparatuses more tightly. Some worry that it is a bad idea.</article>

items.title: Suspected Iran Cyberattacks on U.S. Water Supply Follow Years of Warnings and Neglect
items.author: Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>Federal and state officials are racing to address an assault on the nation’s water supply that they believe is the work of Iranian hackers.</article>

items.title: Abortion Foes Backed Ballot Measures in 2 Red States. Voters Said No.
items.author: Mitch Smith and Ann Hinga Klein
items.content: <article>Voters in Kansas rejected a proposal to start electing Supreme Court justices, while Missourians declined to make it harder to amend the State Constitution.</article>

items.title: Blanche Defends Pirro but Says Trump Can Fire Her at Any Time
items.author: Devlin Barrett
items.content: <article>The head of the Justice Department praised the U.S. attorney in Washington after her tense meeting with the president.</article>

items.title: Can Abdul El-Sayed Unify Michigan Democrats Ahead of the General Election?
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>His close margin of victory may point to challenges ahead.</article>

items.title: Trump Seeks a Boost for Hemp That Would Benefit a Top Aide’s Family
items.author: Kenneth P. Vogel, Christina Jewett and Olivia Diaz
items.content: <article>At the White House’s request, senators tucked a change sought by the hemp industry into a crucial spending bill. It would benefit the son-in-law of Susie Wiles, the president’s chief of staff.</article>

items.title: Muslim Americans Celebrate Abdul El-Sayed’s Win in Michigan Primary
items.author: Madaleine Rubin, Tim Balk, Ama Sarpomaa and Francesca Regalado
items.content: <article>Muslim voters from across the country said they felt hope and anxiety as Dr. El-Sayed moved closer to becoming the nation’s first Muslim senator.</article>

items.title: Shri Thanedar Is Ousted by a Democratic Socialist in a Michigan House Primary
items.author: Bayliss Wagner
items.content: <article>Representative Shri Thanedar is among a wave of Democratic incumbents in Congress whom primary voters have sent packing in a surge of anti-incumbent fervor this cycle.</article>

items.title: Takeaways From the Primary Elections in Michigan
items.author: Reid J. Epstein
items.content: <article>Dr. Abdul El-Sayed narrowly prevailed over Representative Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary for Senate in Michigan, setting up a nervy race to November for the party.</article>
